title: Rethinkg reality: Virtual reality for intensive care and weaning patients - a sequential feasibility and efficacy program
summary:
People who are very ill in the intensive care unit often have many problems.
For example:
• They cannot move.
• They receive very little physical contact.
• They are afraid.
• They have trouble sleeping.
• They are under a lot of stress.
• They are sometimes confused.
Many of these patients are placed on a ventilator.
Once they start feeling better, they need to learn to breathe on their own again.
This is called weaning.
Weaning is exhausting for many people.
They get tired quickly.
They often feel helpless.
They can’t handle much physical exertion.
Virtual reality (VR) can help these people.
VR helps them relax more easily.
It provides them with pleasant sensory experiences.
VR can also motivate and energize them.
The study aims to determine whether VR can be used with patients undergoing weaning.

interventions.name: 1 to at best 3 virtual reality (VR) sessions per patient within 72 hours; session duration is planned to be 10-20 minutes, maximum 30 minutes

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Intensive care treatment or prolonged weaning.
Aware and sufficiently cooperative for supervised VR use.
Ability to communicate discomfort or a desire to stop, either verbally or nonverbally.
Clinically stable condition, as assessed by the treatment team.
Written consent from the patient or the patient’s legal representative
In the case of consent by a legal representative: retroactive patient informed consent as soon as possible
Exclusion criteria:
Acute delirium or impaired judgment with confirmed clinical application.
Known epilepsy or seizure disorder that may be triggered by visual stimuli.
Severe visual, vestibular, or balance disorders with expected VR intolerance.
Known severe motion sickness or previous relevant intolerance to VR.
Clinical instability, e.g., escalating reliance on catecholamines, acute respiratory decompensation, or unexplained deterioration.
Deep sedation or inability to interact.
Other reasons, as determined by a physician, that preclude safe participation.
